citation.title: BRITS: Bidirectional Recurrent Imputation for Time Series
citation.authors: W. Cao, D. Wang, J. Li, H. Zhou, L. Li, Y. Li
citation.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 31 (NeurIPS 2018); supplied text is arXiv preprint v1
citation.pages: unknown (supplied text is the 12-page arXiv preprint)

topic: RNN-based imputation of missing values in multivariate time series (air quality, ICU, activity data)
own_question: How can missing time-series values be imputed and labels predicted jointly, without strong data-generating assumptions?
actual_method_and_evidence: The method uses bidirectional LSTM imputation with a temporal-decay factor and optional cross-feature regression, plus a forward/backward consistency loss. It is trained jointly with a classification head. Evaluation uses artificially masked values (10% of observations) or the STMVL air-quality test protocol, scored by MAE/MRE, with AUC and accuracy for classification. There is no fusion data, no physics diagnostics, and no timing measurement.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: BRITS is bidirectional: imputation at step t uses future observations in the backward pass. That makes it offline and non-causal, so it is not comparable to our strictly-past CES nowcast. It can be cited only as an example of the generic two-sided imputation family.
validation_if_relevant: Validation is by random masking or a month-based test split in non-plasma domains. This is not relevant to our campaign-reuse validation.
forbidden_inferences: Do not present BRITS as a causal nowcaster or real-time estimator
Do not transfer its MAE or AUC results to CES or KSTAR
Do not cite it as evidence about BES/ECEI or impurity Ti
Do not imply our method derives from or improves on BRITS
Do not generalize its imputation setting to all prior time-series work
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional. At most one clause could cite it as a representative learned two-sided (bidirectional) imputation method, to contrast with our causal setting, in the same family as our two-sided interpolation baseline. It is not needed and adds no plasma-specific grounding.
